# Application-profile documentation template

[Contributing](../contributing.md) · [Profile catalogue](../reference/README.md) · [Library documentation standard](../contributing/documentation-standard.md)

Use this checklist when creating or changing a profile page. It is an authoring template, not a configuration to execute. Replace the instructions with concrete facts from the selected profile, adapter and maintained complete example; delete irrelevant guidance. Do not publish blank sections, invented defaults or unsupported examples.

Write for a reader who is new to HomeLab: name who does what, explain necessary terms when first used, and state the concrete result before internal terminology. Keep exact identifiers and technical requirements intact. After editing, reread the complete page, obtain an independent readability review, and revise the prose before calling it complete. Keep each prose paragraph on one source line.

## Purpose and choice

Explain what the application does and when to select this profile rather than another variant. Name the adapter that deploys it and the supporting containers that the app manages. State important external prerequisites in plain language before explaining how HomeLab verifies ownership of an existing installation.

## Syntax and properties

Show the smallest useful app-selection fragment, label it **fragment**, and link its exact app ID in a complete maintained synthetic composition. State which fields belong to the reusable profile and which the user's site configuration must supply.

For each property or binding, document:

- Required, optional or conditional presence, including the requirements enforced by the current adapter.
- The accepted type, any default, limits and allowed values, and important invalid values.
- Named references and their effects. Explain separately which references supply values, require another app to be ready, declare network access, publish a service, establish trust or select account privileges.
- The required interfaces, listeners and published endpoints; storage locations, access and initialization; secrets and authentication; and software and resource requirements.

An absent topic should say “None” or “Not applicable” briefly. Do not add a readiness-column explanation without a table, GUI-password warnings to unrelated apps or fictional secret roles.

## Minimal and practical examples

Link at least one complete canonical YAML source whose references resolve **and** whose deployment packets can be generated by the selected framework using the real library profile. Keep the example body in one source file; check documentation excerpts against it. A catalogue or profile definition alone is not a complete usage example.

Provide fully defined validation commands, or link the setup that defines their shell variables. Explain the expected output, relevant app and guest IDs, and what the example establishes. If an offline example selects retained resources, state that deployment requires an installation already managed by HomeLab; never present it as an installer or import procedure.

Include a practical relationship or variant example where it explains the profile: an explicit upstream service, a managed account, an authentication gateway, multiple interfaces, repeated instances or a deliberate resource override. Explain required companion services without implying every profile is dependency-free.

## First installation

Use this exact heading. Say plainly whether this profile can create a new service and its data, or whether creation is not implemented. Distinguish what source checks and the controller support from installation that has not been verified on the target. Identify vendor setup and any infrastructure, accounts or configuration that must be prepared separately.

For a supported creation path, link its complete example and list its actual prerequisites. Explain that `lifecycle: fresh` is a creation policy which stays unchanged for ordinary later deployments. It is not a one-run switch.

## Later deployments

Use this exact heading. Describe what ordinary deployment maintains and preserves, and which changes may be applied, refused or require a separately reviewed procedure. Distinguish public configuration changes from persistent identity, data and credential changes. `retained` requires an already managed installation; it does not import a foreign one.

State what changes when selected software, images or defaults are updated. Keep version declarations in their existing manifest; do not copy a version policy into a site example or promise automatic upgrades or data migration.

## Invalid cases and validation

Give at least two relevant invalid examples and the intended refusal layer. Trace conditional constraints to the source code and adapter that enforce them. Reuse upstream tests of invalid inputs; add a focused library integration only when it protects a documented composition or known caller requirement.

Maintain profile-to-example coverage in the library's documentation tests. Run the source suite, compile the real examples, check navigation and anchors, and preserve the existing coverage, security, history and signature checks. Distinguish tests of compilation and generated configuration from an authorized continuous deployment (CD) run and checks of the running service.

## Related guidance

Link the profile declaration, complete example, related variant, shared lifecycle and reference pages, and task guides. Preserve useful existing anchors or canonical pointers when replacing old guidance. Review the complete page as a new user before publication.

## Declaration records and effect evidence

Provide stable field destinations for the complete supplied profile definition, including named map objects and their nested fields. Use the normal table of field paths and selected values from [declaration records](../reference/declaration-records.md). Keep pointers connecting definition source to documentation in `tests/documentation_records.py`; do not add a parallel field list. The checker derives fields from source and checks both that new source fields have documentation rows and that removed fields no longer have rows. These rows describe reusable definition values; do not present them as an arbitrary instance override API.

For every nontrivial binding or property, state its type, whether it is required, its default or lack of one, and its allowed values. Explain separately what happens when the value is omitted, null or empty. Name the component that applies the value and explain how it resolves references and handles overrides. Link the exact nested type, prerequisite, complete example and relevant diagnostic where the relationship is explained. Record adapter requirements that exceed profile metadata.

Explain the resulting addresses, ports and identities, the generated configuration, and the effects of explicitly selected dependencies and access rules. Classify ordinary updates, possible interruption, refused changes and unknown behavior separately. Include the exact diagnostic code and context for invalid inputs, along with the supported correction; source compilation does not prove a runtime transition.

Add return links from task guides, diagnostics and examples and retain published destinations. Apply the standard's [review rubric](../contributing/documentation-standard.md#10-verification-and-review-rubric), including a review of meaning and the rendered page; [conformance tests](../testing.md#documentation-conformance) check only the documented parts of this contract automatically.

## Backup coverage

Classify every storage role as authoritative configuration, state or database data, or explicitly exclude it as transient or rebuildable. Link its exact classification and capture requirement in the recovery catalogue. Explain native configuration, individually managed runtime inputs, related databases and the credentials and keys needed for recovery. State what has actually been verified. Installing a client, copying raw database files or copying a running SQLite directory does not prove that the application can be restored.
